newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS - S.Africa rand at new lows - no rate hike yet.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - S.Africa rand at new lows - no rate hike yet.

text.p: The South African rand hit new lows on Monday but Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said he was not contemplating an imminent increase in interest rates.
The battered currency fell to fresh lows against the dollar and British pound, triggering fears of a rate rise and taking its toll on shares and bonds, which fell to a five-month low.

In early afternoon trade, the rand was pegged at 4.6340/90 against the dollar after touching an all-time low of 4.6430 bid on a fresh wave of speculative selling. It also sank to a worst-ever 7.4778 bid against sterling.
However, Stals told Reuters he planned to hold his hand on rates after September money supply data showed some stabilisation.
"It confirms that we maintain the status quo for the time being," Stals said.
"We are looking for indications that it will come down to a lower rate of increase but at least it is encouraging that the rate it is not increasing further."

Broadly defined M3 money supply grew a better-than-expected 14.45 percent in September, down from 15.40 in August, although private credit extension disappointed, expanding by 17.94 percent from 17.70.
Stals had warned in a speech on Friday that already high interest rates might have to be raised further if there was no slowdown in money supply and credit growth.

Dealers said the currency had come under pressure at the opening from London-based dollar buying, a factor cited late last week for the rand's move through the psychologically important 4.60 level for the first time.

Local exporter and offshore dollar selling helped the currency regain some composure by midday, although the market remained wary of a break through 4.65 -- pointed to by technical analysts as the next key resistance point.
The rand has now lost 27 percent of its value against the dollar and 32 percent against sterling since February 15 this year.
Stals said the Reserve Bank had intervened heavily in the foreign exchange market on Friday but the pressure on the currency had eased on Monday.
"On Friday there was quite heavy intervention. This morning it is much less and it looks like the market is stabilising again today," Stals said.
Dealers noted that the Bank had little in its armoury to defend the ailing currency.

South Africa's foreign reserves have been halved in dollar terms since the end of 1995, falling from 15.7 billion rand ($4.3 billion at the prevailing rates) to 10.0 billion rand at the end of September ($2.2 billion), equivalent to just four weeks import cover.
Some traders said the Bank might have little choice but to increase rates by one percentage point if the currency fell below the 4.65 level.
Bank rate, which currently stands at 16 percent, was last hiked by one percentage point on April 26 this year. Commercial banks' prime lending rate currently stands at 19.25 percent.
